node.label: Peter Gay
node.description: A historian of European intellectual and cultural life who joined social history to psychoanalysis. The Enlightenment: An Interpretation (1966, 1969), Weimar Culture (1968) and the five-volume The Bourgeois Experience: Victoria to Freud (1984–98) are his major studies, and Freud: A Life for Our Time (1988) is his biography of Freud. In a 1997 interview he describes Freud as an indispensable resource for studying the interplay of psychological processes and external circumstances, insisting that an event such as the French Revolution still requires attention to state finances, royal prestige and social conflict. He criticized psychohistory that gave inner experience too much causal weight.
node.representative_figures_and_works: The Enlightenment: An Interpretation (two volumes, 1966 and 1969); Weimar Culture (1968); The Bourgeois Experience: Victoria to Freud (five volumes, 1984–1998); Freud: A Life for Our Time (1988).
